---
title: "Playoff seeding"
---

```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
library(ouanalytics)
library(dplyr)
```

`compute_playoff_seeding()` seeds both conferences with the official NBA
tie-break procedure. Teams are ordered by winning percentage. Teams that tie are
separated by these criteria, in order, and the first one that separates them
decides:

1. Head-to-head record (a two-team tie), or record among all the tied teams.
2. Division leader over non-leader.
3. Division record, when the tied teams share a division.
4. Conference record.
5. Record against teams in playoff position in their own conference.
6. Record against teams in playoff position in the other conference.
7. Point differential.

When one team separates from a larger tie, the rest start again at the top of the
list. If nothing separates the teams, they are ordered alphabetically, standing in
for the random draw.

## An example league

The example league has 13 East teams and 6 West teams, with a few games, so some
teams tie.

```{r seeding}
with(seeding_example, compute_playoff_seeding(standings, scores_tidy, meta)) %>%
  filter(conference == "West") %>%
  select(seed, team_name, wins, losses, `Winning Pct`, seed_note)
```

In the West, W1 and W2 tie on winning percentage. W2 won their game, so head-to-head
puts W2 first:

```{r two-team}
with(seeding_example, break_two_team_tie("W1", "W2", NULL, scores_tidy, meta))
```

## The building blocks

```{r blocks}
with(seeding_example, {
  list(
    record = record_vs("W2", c("W1", "W3"), scores_tidy),
    point_differential = point_differential("W2", scores_tidy)
  )
})
```
